speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where your wrist pain is located and when it started, while also telling me more about the fever and any skin lesions you have noticed.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Lyme Arthritis with tenosynovitis).

Given the history of a camping trip in Minnesota, recent self-resolving joint pain, and the classic triad of wrist pain, fever, and chills, I suspect this is Lyme arthritis affecting the left wrist. I am requesting images of the skin lesions to confirm the presence of erythema migrans, and I will order blood work for serology. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_Lesions. REQUEST TEST: Lyme_Serology. REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_Diff.
